summary: Luke Badiali reviewed Meridian's financial model with Chris and Leanne. Utilisation is 68% against a target of 75% and margins vary widely between day-rate and fixed-fee work. We agreed a target pricing model built on fixed-fee workstreams and a cost of acquisition benchmark.

discussion.keyPoints: Average gross margin is 38%, but fixed-fee 100-day work runs at 46%. Chris said day-rate lean work drags the average down.
Week 1 left the £45k fixed fee per workstream as pending. Chris is now more comfortable with it given the margin data, but worried about scope creep.
Leanne estimated partner time on business development at roughly £14k per new client won.

recommendations.recommendation: Price 100-day plans as fixed-fee workstreams from £45k each with a change-control clause, and phase out day rates on PE work.
Set a minimum gross margin of 42% for any engagement before it is signed.
Cap business development cost at £15k per new client, tracked quarterly.
Model a base case of £5.2m fees next year and a downside where one core PE house drops out.

actions.action: Build the margin check into the proposal sign-off

nextFocus: Review the commercial model again after one quarter of live data.
nextPreparation: Leanne to track margin and acquisition cost on every new engagement for the quarter.

tests.question: What pricing model did we agree?
What minimum margin did we agree?
